Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  • Sudden-onset shortness of breath, right-sided pleuritic back pain (began today).  
  • Cough productive of small amounts of blood on two occasions.  
  • Subjective “slight” fever.  
  • Palpitations/awareness of heartbeat.  
  • Two-week history of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.  
  • Underlying systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) treated with methotrexate (immunosuppression and ↑ clot risk).

- Relevant family medical history:  
  • No known family history of venous thrombo-embolism or blood clots.  
  • Other family history not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 45-year-old woman with acute pleuritic pain, dyspnoea, minor haemoptysis and subjective fever on a background of SLE treated with methotrexate. Appears clinically stable on video (normal pulse, normal capillary refill, no cervical lymphadenopathy, normal oropharynx).

Working diagnosis: Suspected community-acquired pneumonia / chest infection.

Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript & DDx:  
• Community-acquired pneumonia – High likelihood given fever, pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, immunosuppression.  
• Pulmonary embolism – Moderate likelihood due to triad of pleuritic pain, SOB, haemoptysis and SLE-related hypercoagulability despite lack of tachycardia or provoking factors.  
• Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis / alveolar haemorrhage – Low-moderate likelihood; patient on methotrexate but onset unusually abrupt.

Management priorities: Urgent face-to-face assessment today for full vital signs, chest auscultation, possible CXR, bloods (FBC, CRP, D-dimer if PE suspected), and treatment (likely antibiotics if infection confirmed).

Management Plan

- Arrange same-day clinic review with GP for:  
  • Full physical examination including auscultation, BP, temperature, respiratory rate, SpO₂.  
  • Baseline observations to assess stability.  
  • Determine need for chest X-ray and laboratory investigations (FBC, U&E, CRP, D-dimer, coagulation profile).  
  • Initiate empiric oral antibiotics if bacterial pneumonia suspected after examination.  
  • Consider hospital referral if vitals unstable or PE strongly suspected.  
  • Reassure patient regarding low immediate likelihood of lung cancer; advise follow-up imaging if symptoms persist.  

- Provide support team phone number to book face-to-face appointment today.

- Patient education: red-flag advice (increasing breathlessness, persistent haemoptysis, high fever, chest pain, syncope) and when to call emergency services.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Offer if anxiety persists – not yet arranged.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Community-acquired pneumonia – High: acute fever, pleuritic pain, cough with minor haemoptysis, immunosuppressed host.  
2. Pulmonary embolism – Moderate: pleuritic pain, dyspnoea, haemoptysis; risk increased by SLE, though vitals currently reassuring.  
3. Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis/alveolar haemorrhage – Low-Moderate: on methotrexate; can present with cough and haemoptysis, but typical course more subacute.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, full immunisation review, alcohol intake, detailed mental health screen, ear and vision screening, urinalysis.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient name alternates between “Tracy Chapman” and “Doris” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Audio adequate; some minor conversational overlaps and name confusion but key clinical information clear.
